Weekend: Trump rejected Iran's conditional proposal to reopen Hormuz; Brent +1.8% to $106.31 Monday and US futures lower (after Friday's close, so not in this data).
MSFT +3.7% Friday (2.1 sigma, 1.6x volume) on a Copilot overhaul (Home, Code, Autopilot); SK Hynix and Samsung down ~4% Monday on Korea's first session back from Chuseok.

sections.overnight: Data = US close Fri 25 Sep, plus SGX/KRX Monday 28 Sep partial sessions as of 12:05 SGT. Tape: SPY +0.5%, QQQ +0.5%, SOXX +1.2% (5d +7.4%), VIX -5.1%, US10Y 5.18% (+2bp), WTI -2.3% (5d -7.9%), gold +0.5%. MSFT +3.66% (2.1 sigma, vol 1.6x): unveiled Copilot Home, Code and Autopilot; Oppenheimer raised its target to $570 (CNBC / Yahoo Finance, 25 Sep). UOB (U11_SI) +2.1% Monday midday (2.0 sigma, vol 0.72x): no reported cause found. SK Hynix (000660_KS) -4.1% and Samsung (005930_KS) -4.3% vs the pre-holiday close, Monday midday: first session after Chuseok; Bloomberg ties Hynix's drop to profit-taking, foreign selling and a report that Solidigm is weighing a US IPO (Bloomberg, 28 Sep). BE +8.3% Friday (1.2 sigma): rebound after the prior session's drop on Oracle's Project Jupiter force-majeure notice; Investing.com credits a Morgan Stanley note, a Yahoo Finance headline says Oracle reaffirmed the 2.4 GW contract (the catalyst recheck due 29 Sep should confirm from the primary source). After the data: Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen Hormuz (Iran sought a blockade lift, sanctions relief and a ceasefire); Brent +1.8% to $106.31, WTI Nov +1.3% to $93.62 Monday (CNBC, 28 Sep); Bloomberg reports the bond selloff resuming.
